reply.text:
Legs fading late in a long run usually comes down to three things: pace, fuel, and how much easy mileage is underneath you. Here is what I would work on.

Run the long run slower than feels necessary. If you can't hold a conversation, it's too fast, and that is the most common reason the last mile falls apart. Build the long run gradually, adding a little each week and dropping back every fourth week. Keep your other runs easy so you arrive at the long run fresh.

Strength work helps here too. Squats, lunges, step-ups, and calf raises twice a week give your legs more reserve when form starts to go.

For anything over about an hour, take in some carbs and fluids during the run. Running out of fuel feels exactly like your legs giving out.

If you want, I can look at your recent runs and see how your pace and distance have been trending. Or I can build you a plan with a progressing long run. How far are you running now, and what are you training for?
